_meta.source: Hawaii PUC Docket 2022-0250 — Energy Equity Docket — Public Comment Tracker (https://puc.hawaii.gov/energy/equity/docket-no-2022-0250-public-comment-tracker/)
_meta.note: These are paraphrased / composite samples of community-side concerns surfaced in the docket and in publicly reported Hawaii energy-equity discussions. Pythia uses them to seed the AI's awareness of what concerns are out there in real Hawaii energy proceedings — they are NOT shown verbatim to participants. Replace with verbatim docket extracts when available.

comments.text: Renters and people without property tax records never see the public-hearing notices. The mail-based notification model misses the people who live closest to the sites.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Native Hawaiian voices and 'Olelo Hawai'i materials are mostly absent from project consultations. When Hawaiian is used, it is symbolic, not substantive.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: We support clean energy. We do not support clean energy projects that bypass community decision-making about which lands are used and how.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: By the time the EIS scoping meeting happens, the site has already been chosen. The decisions that matter — what land, what scale, what footprint — were made before any of us were asked.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: The Community Benefits Package is welcome, but $3,000 per megawatt per year is a small fraction of project revenue and the distribution mechanism is unclear. Who gets to say what 'community priority' means?
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Public comment portals fill with anonymous and out-of-state commenters. There is no way to tell whose voice is whose.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Past consultations have asked for input after the developer had already committed to a site and a design. We had nothing to shape — only something to oppose.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Agricultural-zoned land matters here. Solar on prime ag land is not the same as solar on industrial land. The decision about which land we sacrifice is a community decision, not a developer decision.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: We need reliable power and lower bills as much as anyone. Some projects could deliver that. But we need processes that let us evaluate whether THIS project will, before it's built.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Indigenous governance authorities, where they exist, are routinely sidelined or misrepresented in the consultation record. We are described as 'consulted' when we have not been.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Construction timing matters. Projects that disrupt cultural practice schedules, fishing seasons, or harvest cycles damage trust even when the long-term benefits would be real.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased

comments.text: Translation matters. Materials in 'Olelo Hawai'i are not a courtesy; they are basic respect for the people whose land this is. English-only materials send a message about who is and isn't part of the conversation.
comments.source: Energy Equity Docket — community comment, paraphrased
